Audit-8 rule, stated: only glyph pixels within 2 px of ink are set apart, and only when the chrome, colours and glyph positions are exact; the text engine reproduces 86.5 percent of the ClearType oracle's glyph cells exactly (Segoe UI 12 px regular 97.4, 15 px 92.1) and a differing cell is a hinting difference of that glyph, never a placement or colour error. | Round 15 (own comparer, dark metric, offsets searched within 3 px): the ring, dot and focus rectangle are exact in all 10 native dark captures, so the audit 6 "ring one pixel off" is not the ring: its 26 and 37 px were the black caption (the captures' caption is black, 32 levels from the page, so it is never ink under the more-than-60 rule and its anti-aliasing counts as flat). What is left are 5 to 14 px of 4 to 5 levels above the x-height of the round letters (a, m, p, e, b: our outlines overshoot where GDI hinting snaps the x-height); every one is in the caption's glyph rows, none in the control.
